whyThisShow: This is a pre-Europe '72 warmup at the Academy of Music, officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 14, and the community treats it as a genuine peer to the European run. One listener said the show is "as good as any night in Europe later in the year" and found it "maybe even worth mentioning in the same sentence as the Creamery gig" [source: 'The show is as good as any night in Europe later in the year. Maybe even worth mentioning in the same sentence as the Creamery gig']. It's also a Keith Godchaux introduction night — one reviewer noted that "Phil introduces Keith as the new piano player" [source: 'Phil introduces Keith as the new piano player']. The second set, built around a Truckin' → The Other One → Me and My Uncle → The Other One sequence, is where listeners feel the show earns its reputation, with one calling it simply "MAGICAL" [source: "the '2nd set' gets MAGICAL"]. One listener does flag that "they kinda space at times but when they jam it's blazin'" [source: 'They kinda space at times but when they jam it\'s blazin\'']; that caveat is the minority read on a show the broader community regards as a classic.
listenFor: The second-set Truckin' jam leading into The Other One sequence is the centerpiece — one listener flagged "the jam at the end of Truckin', & then The Other One-> Me & My Uncle-> The Other One" as the highlight [source: 'The jam at the end of Truckin, ,& then The Other One-> Me & My Uncle-> The Other One is really good']. The Stranger (Two Souls in Communion) is a genuine rarity; one reviewer noted being a long-time listener who had "never heard of this song" from the Dead before encountering this show [source: 'it was \'The Stranger\' that caught my attention cuz I\'d never heard of this song. And I\'ve been listening to the Dead for decades']. On the Looks Like Rain, one listener heard Jerry sounding "like he is playing the pedal steel" and called the result "perfectly magical" [source: 'Jerry sounds like he is playing the pedal steel, and it is perfectly magical for this song']. Weir is notably prominent in the mix, something one listener specifically welcomed given the Weir-heavy setlist character of this date [source: 'Mr. Weir mixed right up front where he belongs (particularly on this date!)'].
context: March 26, 1972 at the Academy of Music in New York, just weeks before the band departed for Europe. The recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd1972-03-26.133303.sbd.miller.flac16), transferred by Charlie Miller, and was officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 14. The setlist includes the rarely-played The Stranger (Two Souls in Communion) alongside what would become Europe '72 staples.
funFact: One reviewer, crediting the tape transfer, called Charlie Miller "Time magazine's Man of the year!!!" [source: 'Five huge stars for Charlie Miller (Time magazine\'s Man of the year!!!)']
headline: That Other One at the Academy, days before Europe.
